verdict_reason: Page metadata field set and semantics are correct and well tested, but the record carries no @Schema annotations so the generated OpenAPI drops the required/minimum constraints the locked contract declares.

todos.issue: No @Schema on the record or any component, so springdoc emits OperatorPageResponse with no 'required' array, no descriptions and no minimum bounds (docs/openapi/operators.yml lines 329-346) while the locked contract's OperatorPage declares items/page/page_size/total_items/total_pages all required with minimums (api-contract.locked.yaml lines 589-614); the compliance IT's divergence gate only compares path set + operationIds so the drift is unenforced.
todos.fix: Add @Schema(description=...) on the record and @Schema(description=..., requiredMode = Schema.RequiredMode.REQUIRED, minimum=...) on each of items/page/pageSize/totalItems/totalPages, matching the locked contract's minimums (page>=1, pageSize>=1, totalItems>=0, totalPages>=0).

todos.issue: The compact constructor null-guards items with Objects.requireNonNull but does not defensively copy it, so the record advertised as immutable keeps a live reference to whatever List the caller passed (OperatorService today passes an immutable Stream.toList(), but nothing enforces that on future callers or tests).
todos.fix: Replace Objects.requireNonNull(items, "items") with items = List.copyOf(items); it both null-guards (List.copyOf throws NPE on null) and makes the component genuinely unmodifiable.
